source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Frames an LLM agent as a case-based reasoner. A case bank holds (state, action, reward) tuples. A planner LLM reads retrieved cases; the executor LLM stays frozen. Reached top place on GAIA validation.
numbers: GAIA validation 87.88% Pass@3 (GPT-4.1 planner, o3 executor); GAIA test 79.40%; DeepResearcher 66.6 F1 / 80.4 PM; SimpleQA 95.0%; HLE 24.4 PM.
limits: Case bank on GAIA was built during validation; test used that bank. Heavy tool use, so gains are not from retrieval alone. Headline numbers have no clean no-memory arm on GAIA.
agent_relevance: Closest published match to our subgoal library: store solved cases, retrieve by similarity, keep the model frozen.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Number of retrieved cases K matters little and peaks early. A small, high-quality memory beats a large one.
quote: CBR benefits from a small, high-quality memory, unlike few-shot prompting
limits: One planner/executor pair (GPT-4.1 / o4-mini). Gain of about 4.6 F1 points from K=0 to K=4, then a plateau.
agent_relevance: Retrieve 1 to 4 cases, not many. Unlike few-shot prompting, more cases did not help.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Five-iteration continual learning on DeepResearcher: case memory helps a little over no CBR; a learned (parametric) retriever helps a little more.
limits: Margin over no-CBR shrinks: +1.2 at iter 1 to +0.4 at iter 5 (non-parametric). The no-CBR arm also improves each round, so the retrieval share is small.
agent_relevance: Honest size of the retrieval effect on top of a strong agent is under 1 point late. Do not expect large gains from a case library alone.

source: Guo et al. (2026) CASCADE: Case-Based Continual Adaptation for LLMs During Deployment
finding: Treats case retrieval as a contextual bandit: explore cases of uncertain value, exploit proven ones. Full CBR cycle (retrieve, reuse and revise, retain).
numbers: 16 tasks (medical, legal, code, web, tool use, embodied). Macro-average success +20.9% over zero-shot. Average success 63.76% (plain similarity CBR, NP-CBR) to 66.68% (CASCADE) on Qwen3-32B; about 3% relative over NP-CBR with gemini-2.0-flash.
limits: Gain of CASCADE over plain similarity retrieval is about 3 points. Qwen3 family plus one API model. Needs binary reward feedback. Authors' own benchmark choice.
agent_relevance: Learned retrieval value beats pure similarity by a small, consistent margin. Our S9 record could carry a success count per case.

source: Guo et al. (2026) CASCADE: Case-Based Continual Adaptation for LLMs During Deployment
finding: Memory beat weight updates: CASCADE beat REINFORCE+LoRA on 9 of 12 tasks (comparable on the rest); with 4 retrieved cases it also beat it on the remaining 3. Needs under 4 GB GPU memory.
numbers: 9 of 12 tasks at k=1; 12 of 12 at k=4. CASCADE lower bound above zero-shot upper bound in 9 of 12 tasks across Qwen3 4B to 32B.
limits: Fails when the base model never succeeds: on MIMIC-IV medication recommendation with Qwen3-4B all methods failed. Only successes are stored; failures are discarded (authors flag as future work).
agent_relevance: Case reuse needs a base model that can already succeed sometimes. Supports keeping a strong model in the loop.

source: Guo et al. (2026) CASCADE: Case-Based Continual Adaptation for LLMs During Deployment
finding: Ablation: other bandit algorithms (LinLogUCB, NeuralLogUCB, NeuralLinUCB) varied a lot by task; the authors' Neural-LinLogUCB was best or comparable on all tasks. Exploration coefficient 0.1 to 1.0 gave positive gains over NP-CBR in most settings.
numbers: Single numbers shown only in figures (Fig 4c, 4d), not recoverable from text.
limits: Authors' own method wins their own ablation; no independent replication found.
agent_relevance: Retrieval policy is task-dependent. Test retrieval design on our own tasks.

source: Hatalis et al. (2025) Review of Case-Based Reasoning for LLM Agents
finding: Review mapping the classic Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain cycle (Aamodt and Plaza 1994) onto LLM agents; links to Goal-Driven Autonomy, cognitive architectures and metacognition. Conceptual; no new experiments.
numbers: Quotes prior reports only: DS-Agent 100% development-stage success and 99% one-pass in deployment with GPT-4; case-based GDA beating rule-based GDA in game environments.
quote: The standard CBR process includes four main
limits: Position paper. Claims that CBR reduces hallucination are argued, not measured.
agent_relevance: Vocabulary bridge between Kolodner/Schank and our schema. Do not cite it as evidence of effect size.

source: Guo et al. (2024) DS-Agent: Automated Data Science by Empowering LLMs with Case-Based Reasoning (ICML)
finding: First large LLM-agent system built on the CBR cycle. Case bank holds Kaggle solutions. Development stage: retrieve, reuse, revise with execution feedback, retain. Deployment stage: one-shot retrieve and adapt code.
numbers: Development: GPT-4 100% success over 12 tasks. Deployment (18 tasks, 10 runs): one-pass rate nearly 100% (99.44) with GPT-4; 85% with GPT-3.5; +25 points over zero-shot with Mixtral-8x7b. Cost $1.60 per run (dev) and $0.13 (deploy) with GPT-4.
limits: Cases are expert Kaggle reports, not the agent's own history. Tabular ML tasks with a code runner. Authors' own benchmark.
agent_relevance: Retrieving expert cases then revising from real execution output matches our G2 (revise only from real output).

source: Guo et al. (2024) DS-Agent: Automated Data Science by Empowering LLMs with Case-Based Reasoning (ICML)
finding: Ablations: both retrieval and revision-from-feedback matter. A random case (one-shot) helped less than retrieval, and for GPT-3.5 one-shot did not beat zero-shot.
numbers: Development, GPT-4, average best rank (lower is better): full 2.08; w/o ReviseRank (top retrieved case used unchanged) 2.58; w/o CBR 3.41. Five repeats.
limits: Authors say one-shot is generally better than zero-shot except GPT-3.5. Individual deployment bar values are partly garbled in the extract.
agent_relevance: A mismatched or unadapted case can fail to help weaker models. A reject-or-adapt rule for retrieved cases is justified.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners (AAAI)
finding: Agent gathers success and failure trajectories, extracts text insights, and retrieves similar past trajectories by task similarity. Task-similarity retrieval beat reason-similarity retrieval, and random selection dropped performance significantly.
numbers: ALFWorld ablation of example selection: task similarity best, reason similarity a noticeable dip, random a significant drop (exact Table 3 numbers not recoverable from text). FEVER transfer from HotpotQA: ReAct 58, ExpeL transfer 65 +/- 1.7, with task demos 70 +/- 0.7.
limits: Insight ablations done only on HotpotQA. Insights from gpt-3.5 were worse than from gpt-4. Adding reflections to insight generation hurt.
agent_relevance: Retrieve by task similarity, not by the latest reasoning step. Pair raw cases with abstracted insights.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners (AAAI)
finding: Retrieval and insights are complementary; with Reflexion retries both climb. On WebShop the two parts were a near tie.
numbers: ALFWorld success by Reflexion round R0 to R3: ExpeL retrieve-only 40.3, 47.8, 52.2, 54.4%; ExpeL+Reflexion rows 54.5, 57.5, 59.7, 60.4% and 59.0, 60.4, 63.4, 64.2% (row labels unclear in extract). WebShop insights-only 37% vs retrieve-only 38%.
limits: Row labels in the extracted Table 2 are ambiguous. Diversity of success/failure data from Reflexion beat ReAct-only data.
agent_relevance: Failure cases paired with successes support better abstractions than successes alone.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Induces reusable workflows (abstract subgoal routines) from past trajectories and keeps them in memory. Close to a library of abstracted cases.
numbers: WebArena (gpt-4): +51.1% relative success over the best published autonomous baseline (BrowserGym, 23.5), so about 35.5; +7.6 to 7.9% relative over a method with human-written workflows. Mind2Web cross-task step success +24.6% relative. Gap over baselines grows by 8.9 to 14.0 absolute points as train-test distance widens.
limits: Some table cells garbled in extract. Gains largest where tasks share structure. ReasoningBank (2026) later found AWM gave no gain or degraded on cross-website tasks.
agent_relevance: Abstracting cases into workflows is what a subgoal library needs. Check cross-domain transfer separately.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: Experience-Following Behavior
finding: Names the experience-following property. When the new task is close to a stored case, the agent's output is close to the stored output. Good if the case is right, bad if it is wrong.
numbers: Four agents (EHRAgent, AgentDriver, RegAgent synthetic, CIC-IoT); also GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3. Output similarity rises with input similarity in all addition-based memories; the fixed-memory baseline stays low on both.
limits: Shows copying, not adapting, which is the weak form of the Revise step. Correlational measure.
agent_relevance: Models copy near cases. A wrong case is most dangerous exactly when it looks most similar. Add a check before reuse.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: Experience-Following Behavior
finding: Error propagation: bad stored executions are retrieved, copied and stored again. Performance lags an error-free-memory control at once; the gap grows with indiscriminate or coarse-evaluator addition.
numbers: With a strict evaluator, history-based deletion can beat the error-free-memory control. With a coarse or noisy evaluator, deletion does not help. Tables not recoverable cell by cell.
limits: Needs a trustworthy utility evaluator.
agent_relevance: Retain only cases that passed a code-checked test (G3). Use later task outcomes as free quality labels.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: Experience-Following Behavior
finding: Misaligned experience replay: cases that passed the quality filter can still mislead on the current task. Deleting by downstream utility helps. Under task distribution shift, periodic deletion stabilises performance.
numbers: Deleted records had higher prediction error than retained ones (KDE, RegAgent). Fixed capacity 100 records (EHRAgent) and 180 (AgentDriver): managed memory kept high performance vs fixed baseline.
limits: Small memory sizes; four agent tasks only.
agent_relevance: A case library needs forgetting. Links to the case-base maintenance sibling subfield.

source: Sarukkai et al. (2025) Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents for Sequential Decision-Making Tasks
finding: Storing the agent's own successful trajectories and retrieving top-k by cosine similarity of goals gives large gains. Curating the database adds more.
numbers: gpt-4o-mini, 5 seeds: ALFWorld 73% to 89%; Wordcraft 55% to 64%; InterCode-SQL 75% to 79%. ALFWorld gain (15 points) equals upgrading gpt-4o-mini to gpt-4o. With database-level plus exemplar-level curation, ALFWorld 93%.
limits: Diminishing returns: most gain in first 25% of added tasks. Within-run dips show some added trajectories hurt. Early database-quality estimates are noisy.
agent_relevance: A self-built library of verified successes is cheap and worth about a model upgrade. Curate it.

source: Sarukkai et al. (2025) Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents for Sequential Decision-Making Tasks
finding: Utility-based exemplar curation: keep trajectories by how well they work as examples. Best-ranked beat worst-ranked at every database size on ALFWorld and Wordcraft.
numbers: Best vs worst (bottom-1) curves in Fig 4: best higher at all sizes for ALFWorld and Wordcraft; only at small sizes for InterCode-SQL. Final ALFWorld above AutoManual (0.79, hand-designed spaces, stronger LLM).
limits: Exemplar curation helped SQL and Wordcraft most; database-level curation helped ALFWorld. Gains are task-dependent.
agent_relevance: Score each stored case by outcome when reused: the retain step with a quality gate.

source: Ouyang et al. (2026) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
finding: Stores distilled strategies from both successes and failures instead of raw trajectories. Beats raw-trajectory memory (Synapse) and workflow memory (AWM).
numbers: WebArena overall success +8.3, +7.2, +4.6 points over no-memory with three backbones; up to 20% relative gain and up to 16% fewer interaction steps. One split: No Memory 39.0, Synapse 40.6, AWM 44.4.
limits: AWM and Synapse gave no gain or degraded on the cross-website (Multi) subset. An LLM judge labels success, so labels are noisy.
agent_relevance: Abstract strategy items from failures as well as wins; raw case replay transfers worst across domains.

source: Wei et al. (2026) Evo-Memory: Benchmarking LLM Agent Test-time Learning with Self-Evolving Memory
finding: Benchmark of 10+ memory modules on task streams. Simple retrieval (ExpRAG, similar past task experience) is a strong baseline. Gain from memory tracks within-dataset task similarity.
numbers: ReMem gain over history baseline vs within-dataset task similarity: Pearson r = 0.717 (Gemini 2.5 Flash), 0.563 (Claude 3.7 Sonnet). Big gains on PDDL and ALFWorld; small on AIME-25 and GPQA. Baselines degrade when failures are stored unfiltered.
limits: Correlation across few datasets. Smaller models benefit most.
agent_relevance: Case reuse pays when tasks recur in structure; on diverse reasoning sets expect little. Filter failures before storing.

source: Yang et al. (2024) Buffer of Thoughts
finding: Retrieves a stored high-level thought template from a meta-buffer and instantiates it for the new problem. A CBR-style reuse of abstract cases.
numbers: Game of 24: GPT-4 3.0%, ToT 74.0, BoT 82.4. Checkmate-in-One: GPT-4 36.4, ToT 49.2, BoT 86.4. Geometric Shapes 93.6 vs 52.6. Date Understanding 88.2 vs 68.4.
limits: Authors' own template buffer, possibly close to the test distribution. No independent replication seen here.
agent_relevance: Large gains on tasks with a reusable algorithmic template; supports a template-level library alongside raw cases.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with LLMs
finding: Skill library of verified executable programs in a vector database keyed by embedding of the skill description, retrieved for new tasks. A working library of verified subgoal solutions.
numbers: 3.3x more unique items, 2.3x longer distances, tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior state of the art in Minecraft. Skills transferred to a new world.
limits: Minecraft only; retrieval by description similarity; a skill is added only after a verifier confirms success.
agent_relevance: Strong precedent: store verified, executable subgoal solutions and retrieve by text similarity.

source: Suzgun et al. (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
finding: The model keeps and rewrites a cheatsheet of reusable strategies and code during the run. Big gains when one reusable solution transfers across items.
numbers: GPT-4o Game of 24 about 10% to 99% after it stored a Python solution; Claude 3.5 Sonnet AIME 2024 23% to 50%, AIME 2025 +30 points; GPQA-Diamond +9%; MMLU-Pro Engineering and Physics +8%.
limits: The Game of 24 jump is reuse of one code solution, not similarity retrieval; gains are smaller on diverse sets.
agent_relevance: Reusing a verified program is the best case for a library. Gains drop where no single reusable item exists.

source: Wiratunga et al. (2024) CBR-RAG: Case-Based Reasoning for Retrieval Augmented Generation in LLMs for Legal Question Answering
finding: Uses CBR indexing and similarity to retrieve cases (question, answer, support text) for legal QA. Compared BERT, LegalBERT and AnglE-BERT embeddings and hybrid weights [0.25, 0.40, 0.35].
numbers: Mistral-7B, cosine to reference answer: No-RAG 0.8967; best hybrid AnglE-BERT k=3 full case 0.9141 (+1.94%). Significant vs No-RAG at 95% and vs hybrid BERT k=1 only at 90%.
limits: Very small absolute gain; baseline already high from parametric memory; metric is embedding cosine, not human or factual grading. One dataset (Australian legal QA).
agent_relevance: Case representation (problem, solution, support) helped a little; do not expect large gains from better embeddings alone.

source: Aamodt and Plaza (1994) Case-based reasoning: foundational issues, methodological variations, and system approaches
finding: Defines the four-step cycle Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain, the base of later CBR agent papers.
numbers: No numbers (conceptual framework).
limits: Not opened this session; known through the Hatalis review.
agent_relevance: Maps to our S9 record: retrieve, reuse, revise (only from real output), retain (only if checked).

source: Hammond (1986) CHEF: A model of case-based planning (AAAI)
finding: Early CBR planner for recipes. Retrieves a past plan by anticipated failures, repairs it, and stores the repaired plan indexed by the failure it learned about.
numbers: No numbers recalled with confidence.
limits: Not opened; detail from memory only.
agent_relevance: Index cases by the failure they avoid, not only by surface similarity.

source: Smyth and Keane (1998) Adaptation-guided retrieval: questioning the similarity assumption in reasoning
finding: Argued that the most similar case is not always the most adaptable; retrieve by cost of adaptation.
numbers: No numbers recalled.
limits: Not opened; from memory.
agent_relevance: Rank retrieved cases by how little must change, not only by how alike they look.
